Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · Church life

sign noun

a mark, an indication

also signal, mark, token, indication, make a sign, make the sign of the cross, sign of the cross, cross oneself

classical

Liv. 21.58.2: ad prīma ac dubia signa vēris
Quint. 1.3.1: ingeniī signum in parvīs praecipuum memoria est

signum, signī n.

noun, second declension

sign, mark, signal

Of a mark, a token, an omen and a signal: signum dare, to give the signal. The sign of the cross is signum crucis; to cross oneself, sē signāre (M-O s.v. cross oneself).

Other words

  • indicium, indiciī n. — sign, evidence (of something)

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Quint. 5.9.9 (Lewis & Short)

    A sign from which something else is understood, as a crime from blood (Quint.).

  • nūtus, nūtūs m. — a nod, a sign with the head

    noun, fourth declension · also used · classical · Ov. Tr. 2.453: digitīsque saepe est nūtūque locūtus (Lewis & Short); Phaedr. App. 28.7–10: dexteram dēmōnstrat nūtū partem

    Of signing with the head instead of speaking.

Examples

  • ad prīma ac dubia signa vēris

    at the first, uncertain signs of springLiv. 21.58.2

  • ingeniī signum in parvīs praecipuum memoria est

    in little children the chief sign of talent is memoryQuint. 1.3.1

  • fac, cum vocante somnō castum petis cubīle, frontem locumque cordis crucis figūra signet

    when sleep calls and you seek your chaste bed, let the sign of the cross mark your forehead and your heartPrud. Cath. 6.129–132

  • pollice signum crucis pingō in fronte

    I make the sign of the cross on my forehead with my thumb (a boy describing his morning)Erasm. Coll., Pietās puerīlis

See also sign, sign, bow.

SourcesLewis & Short: signum · Lewis & Short: indicium · Lewis & Short: nutus
